description:
The United States has launched a seventh consecutive night of air strikes on Iran, targeting military and infrastructure sites across the country's south and centre.

Iranian officials report casualties following attacks in Hormozgan province, while Tehran has warned that continued US strikes could trigger a broader offensive. Iran's armed forces say they have launched drone attacks targeting US military assets in Kuwait and Jordan.

The escalating conflict has also heightened tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route, as diplomatic efforts to prevent a wider regional war continue.

Al Jazeera's correspondents report from Tehran, Washington and Doha.

description:
US President Donald Trump has renewed claims of widespread election fraud, releasing declassified documents and ordering new investigations into alleged vulnerabilities in the US electoral system.

The White House says the documents reveal evidence of election security concerns, while critics argue voter fraud remains extremely rare and accuse Trump of undermining confidence ahead of the midterm elections.

Independent studies and bipartisan organisations have found only a tiny fraction of voter registrations involve non-citizens.

Al Jazeera's Patty Culhane reports from Washington, DC.

description:
Smoke from Canada's massive wildfires has spread across the northeastern United States, triggering air quality alerts in New York, Chicago and Washington, DC.

More than 850 wildfires are burning across Canada, with over 100 classified as out of control. Authorities have evacuated railway workers trapped by advancing flames in Ontario.

The smoke has raised concerns ahead of the FIFA Club World Cup final, set to take place in the New York area on Sunday, with officials closely monitoring air quality.

Al Jazeera's Kristen Saloomey reports from New York.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Brazil is considering its response after the United States announced new 25% tariffs on thousands of Brazilian products, with the measures due to take effect next week.

The tariffs have intensified political tensions ahead of Brazil’s presidential election, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government accusing Washington of unfair pressure.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio blamed Lula for the trade dispute, while Brazilian officials rejected the remarks as unacceptable.

The tariffs are expected to affect nearly a fifth of Brazil’s exports to the United States, although key products including coffee, beef and orange juice are exempt.

Al Jazeera’s Monica Yanakiew reports from Rio de Janeiro.
